You will be guided in using AI to support your learning journey.

Read the topic on "Communicating with AI".

Link to AI notes


You are in the wonderful era of Artificial Intelligence where AI has the super knowledge to help you with many tasks, including coding. But, will AI replace you completely and render you useless? Let's find out!

You wanted to create a calculator that can perform addition(+), subtraction(-), division(/) and multiplication(x) with 2 numbers.

The program will ask the user to key in the formula, e.g. 5x3. IT will then display the answer. The program will run forever.

Follow the test format below.

Test Input

1+3 1.05 + 2.555 4-2 10 /3 5.0 / 0 3 x 5.5

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below:

Example 1 Enter a formula (e.g., 5x3): 1+3 4.0 Enter a formula (e.g., 5x3): 1.05 + 2.555 3.605 Enter a formula (e.g., 5x3): 4-2 2.0 Enter a formula (e.g., 5x3): 10 /3 3.333333333 Enter a formula (e.g., 5x3): 5.0 / 0 Invalid input formula Enter a formula (e.g., 5x3): 3 x 5.5 16.5 . . .the program runs on


What you can learn from this exercise:

1. All AI models have limitations. The answer may not be perfect, especially when it has not been specifically trained with very similar data.

2. You may get lucky and receive a correct answer on the first try. Most of the time, you may have to interact a few rounds to tweak the answer.







.

You have in mind a game that looks like the following example:


Try using an AI model to help you create the game that runs like the sample.


What you can learn from this exercise:

1. In order for the AI model to create a program that you want, you need to know how to describe it clearly so that it produces the right answer. This is call prompt engineering.

2. In real-life problem, nobody will be giving you a detailed problem description that is convenient to be posted to an AI model for an answer. As a programmer, you are the one to direct the AI to produce the right answer.





.
